Sam T: Heads-up - FinServX pilot wants BYO-KMS + optional escrow to neutral HSM vendor. They pushed for a documented key ceremony and a 7-day emergency rotate SLA. Can we outline what we can commit in the POC?
Marta (Legal): need to see proposed escrow clause. Also flag: customer asked for indemnity language if escrow release is misused. We'll likely need an approval matrix.
Noah (PS): POC scope question: do they expect full dataset re-encryption during emergency rotate or just new writes? Their infra lead was ambiguous.
Esha (Security): security questionnaire items to prefill: key lifecycle, split custody, role-based approvals, HSM vendor certs (FIPS), audit log retention, chain-of-custody for escrow. I can draft answers once we confirm process.
Rao (Infra): network note - for on-prem HSM peering we need their egress IPs, MTU constraints, and any firewall ACLs. Also, CloudHSM vs Luna changes provisioning time.
Sam T: FinServX prefers cloud HSM for latency but legal is pushing escrow as a fallback. They want automatic billing visibility for rotate events.
billing-bot: FYI - we can emit webhooks for event:rotation.completed and rotation.requested. Doc: https://redwood.internal/billing/events#rotation
Marta (Legal): escrow redline requests: (1) escrow-holder must be SOC2 + annual audit, (2) release requires 2-person authorization from customer + Redwood legal sign-off, (3) escrow access audit trail immutable for 7 years.
Noah (PS): operational estimate: initial POC integrate + one emergency rotate (cloud-HSM) ~ 10-18 hrs infra + 6 hrs ops playbook prep. If we automate rotates it'll be 3-5 hrs per incident. On-prem HSM adds 8-10 hrs for network/runbook work.
Esha (Security): propose two SOW modes: Forward-only rotate (new traffic uses new keys; historical data untouched) OR Backfill re-encryption (we re-encrypt past artifacts). Backfill has bigger cost & longer window. Need customer's preference.
Sam T: please draft both options. For pricing, I'd rather show a deterministic band not open-ended.
Noah (PS): suggested pricing model: Dedicated base includes 1 emergency rotate per 6 months. Additional emergency rotates: $9k/rotate (covers infra ops + token reprocessing up to X tokens). Backfill re-encryption billed at $Y per million tokens. Escrow setup $Z + annual custody fee.
Rao (Infra): engineering blocker: cached embeddings and KV stores may need full CPU reprocess to re-encrypt. Recommend offering a migration playbook that does staged backfill to minimize hotspotting.
Esha (Security): also confirm key-rotation notification workflow: we should send rotation.pre-hook to customer's security webhook, rotation.completed webhook, plus signed attestation that keys were rotated and old keys revoked. That helps compliance.
Sam T: good. Add billing webhook on rotation.completed to their billing contact.
Marta (Legal): also need to set SLA remedies. If we miss 7-day emergency rotate, what credit or remediation? propose service credit tiered by delay.
Noah (PS): agree. For POC leave penalty language light; escalate for enterprise contract.
Sam T: action items: Noah - draft SOW two-mode rotation clauses + pricing bands. Marta - redline escrow release and SLA penalty proposal. Esha - draft questionnaire answers and attach KMS architecture diagram. Rao - infra hours + bill-integration estimate. I'll schedule follow-up call with customer's CISO and infra lead tomorrow.
Noah (PS): sample SOW snippet Ill include:
```
Rotation SLA: Redwood will complete an authorized emergency key rotation within 7 calendar days. Options: Forward-only (no historical re-encryption) or Backfill (full re-encryption per Appendix B timeline). Billing: See Appendix C.
Escrow: Customer may elect third-party escrow. Escrow releases require documented authorization per Section 4 and Redwood legal concurrence.
```
Sam T: thanks everyone. I'll send the draft materials to FinServX and include these options. :thumbsup:
